**Taxonomy.** Nine classes:
- script or language leak
- encoding damage
- degeneration
- fabricated reference
- fabricated evidence
- instruction loss
- behavioural drift
- context-integrity loss
- inconsistency under resampling

**Measured baseline**
- The operator's symptom is already in our log: 8 event records contain Russian words leaked into English, dated 2026-10-24 21:05 to 2026-10-25 08:44. They carry no model id or context fill, so I filed bug Bb54029aee9.
- 10,326 commit messages have zero foreign-script letters.
- 3,388 tracked files hold 128 foreign letters in 11 files, and 2 of the 11 are real drift.
- Across 107,146 events, mixed Latin+Cyrillic words had 100% precision (n=2).
- A naive "any non-ASCII" rule flags at least 815 files for 2 real hits, under 0.3% precision.
- 997 Claude transcripts (93,770 API calls, all Claude models) show no text drift up to the 950K bucket.
- There is no DeepSeek data on this host, so its drift curve is unknown.

**Best detectors:** script and mixed-word checks with allowlists and quoted-text exemptions; invisible, bidi, replacement and mojibake characters; checks that paths, ids, flags and symbols named in output actually exist; mismatch between reports and gate evidence; a context-integrity canary (about 1K tokens, scored against ddflow's own records); and per-model behavioural counters. Raw tool-error and re-edit rates are dominated by confounds, so only within-task changes count.

**Recovery.** A five-level ladder: note, warn, checkpoint, quarantine, rotate.
- Quarantined commits cannot merge until re-reviewed, and `ddflow bisect` finds the onset.
- The summary seed comes from the event log, git and gate state, and the agent's own note is validated against it.
- ddflow closes the lane and opens a fresh one with the seed, brief, decisions and recording access, resuming from the last green commit.
- The lead cannot be closed by ddflow, so it gets the same pack plus advice (compact with ddflow-written instructions, or a new session re-grounded from `brief`).

**Per-model policy.** A catalog fact `drift_onset_tokens` (source, confidence, samples, expiry) separate from the advertised window. It can only lower the D-CC-Q4 and TE-context-caps marks, and company floors tighten-only. The learner estimates onset per (served model, harness) over 50K fill buckets, and only ever lowers it automatically. Raising needs opt-in and bounded steps. Exploration is off by default, with sandbox canary probes first. The synthetic demo converges to 350K from a prior of 600K, and holds at 300K when exploration overshoots. I found no vendor statement on DeepSeek V3.2 or V4 degradation or language mixing (the DeepSeek-V4-Pro card (preview) only recommends a 384K window for Think Max), so the 350K figure stays your observation.

**Recommendation: option B.** Deterministic detectors, canaries, per-model thresholds, and rotation with a ground-truth summary. Option A (prompt-only) fails because the drifted agent is the one reading the instruction. Option C (second-model and sampling checks) is limited to diffs the detectors flagged. B is invalidated if DeepSeek drift turns out to be mostly same-script semantic errors, or if models pass the canary while drifting.

**Queued:** phase P-drift with 19 tasks, priority 25, wave-tagged, no cycles, small globs. Waves are in `docs/ddflow/decisions/hallucination-drift.md`, including the three you asked for (HAL-learn-onset, HAL-explore, HAL-fact-records).
- Wave 1: HAL-decide, HAL-baseline-scan, HAL-detect-script, HAL-model-facts
- Wave 2: HAL-detect-refs, HAL-signals, HAL-canary, HAL-fact-records
- Wave 3: HAL-ladder, HAL-hook, HAL-gate, HAL-digest, HAL-rotate, HAL-learn-onset, HAL-measure
- Wave 4: HAL-lead-recover, HAL-explore, HAL-e2e, HAL-docs
- Also linked as related: DRV-model-catalog, CC-inventory, CC-resume-pack, DX-handoff-pack, SW-seed-pack, SW-ledger, TE-measure, B-am-ingest, TE-context-caps.
- "CC-seed" does not exist; SW-seed-pack is the nearest.

**Other findings**
- The importer decision for hidden-Unicode checks has no implementation I could find.
- Every Bash call prints `exa: command not found`, a host alias problem, not a ddflow one.

**Open questions with defaults for you to ask the operator**
- Priority: HIGH, wave 1 now.
- Allowed scripts: Latin only, plus a per-project list.
- Enforcement: refuse invisible or bidi characters, warn on foreign letters.
- Canary: on for unknown-family models and models with a recorded onset.
- DeepSeek rotate mark: 300K.
- Learning: lower automatically, raise off.
- Exploration: off in release 1.
- Lead: advice only, never an automatic clear.
- Sharing learned facts across projects: off.
- Language-ID models (lingua, fastText): not in release 1.
- Detector hits: findings for review-style hits, bugs only when committed code is defective.</result>

data.how: In a worktree: 'uv run ruff format <files> && uv run ruff check <files>' before 'git commit'; for a merge conflict resolution re-run it on the merged files; when fixing a Bci-ruff-* bug run 'uv run ruff format .' only on the failing files and commit it separately with a short message; 'ddflow precommit' runs the project's hooks if you want the exact CI set.
data.rule: Before committing or running the item's gates, run 'uv run ruff format <touched files>' and 'uv run ruff check <touched files>'; put pure formatting changes in their own commit. Agents must not leave formatting to the pre-push hook or to CI.
data.title: Run ruff format (and ruff check) on the Python files you touched before every commit
data.why: On 2026-10-24..26 the CI Lint step and the pre-push stage failed repeatedly on 'ruff format --check' and 'ruff check' (an unused variable in a test, unformatted files after merges), found only at push time or by an unlucky agent's ci; each cost a red main, a bug, and an agent run. ruff format is deterministic and takes under a second.

data.body: Operator asked 2026-10-26 to prevent ruff-format failures. Options: a pre-commit hook that formats staged Python files with ruff format (fix mode, restage), ddflow merge running ruff format on the merged diff's Python files as a bot commit, a gate check in standards, and a line in the agent brief (L-format-python-before-commit). Decide the least surprising combination; keep derived formatting out of review diffs (D-lean-review risk tiers).
data.title: Auto-format touched Python files at commit/merge time (ruff format) and make the agent brief say so, so ruff format --check never fails at push time
